name: San Marino
summary: Own law (L. 139/1997): possessing drugs without intent to sell, and personal use, are crimes (6 months–3 years, reducible); adults with under 3 g of cannabis face a day-fine. Tables updated Sept 2026.
poisonControlNote: No national poison centre; the nearest are Italian centres (e.g. Milan Niguarda, +39 02 6610 1029, 24h).
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Personal use is a crime (unless prescribed via ISS), so police involvement is possible. Failing to help someone in danger is a crime (Penal Code art. 162).

lsd.note: Table I: possession without intent to sell, or use, is a crime (6 months–3 years' prison; can be reduced to 3–12 months if minor; judicial pardon possible).

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin, psilocin and Psilocybe, Conocybe and Stropharia fungi are Table I: possession or use is a crime (6 months–3 years, reducible).

dmt.note: DMT and ayahuasca (incl. harmine/harmaline) are Table I: possession or use is a crime (6 months–3 years, reducible).

mescaline.note: Mescaline and peyote (Lophophora williamsii) are Table I: possession or use is a crime (6 months–3 years, reducible).

dox.note: DOM, DOB and DOC are Table I: possession or use is a crime (6 months–3 years, reducible).

nbomes.note: 25I-, 25B-, 25C-NBOMe and analogues are Table I: possession or use is a crime.

2c-x.note: 2C-B, 2C-I and analogues are Table I: possession or use is a crime (6 months–3 years, reducible).

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2, 2C-T-7 and 2C-T-21 are listed in Table I: possession or use is a crime.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT, 5-MeO-MiPT and 5-MeO-DiPT are listed in Table I: possession or use is a crime.

cannabis.note: Adults with under 3 g (no intent to sell): minor offence, day-fine (20–60 days). Larger amounts or a repeat within 5 years: 6 months–3 years.

ketamine.note: Licensed medicine listed in Table I: legal only with an ISS-recognised prescription; otherwise possession or use is a crime (6 months–3 years).

mxe.note: Methoxetamine is Table I: possession or use is a crime.

dxm.note: Expressly excluded from the 2026 drug tables; sold as a cough medicine.

nitrous.note: Not in the 2026 drug tables; no specific rule found.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are Table I: possession or use is a crime. ADHD stimulants are prescription-only medicines.

mdma.note: Table I: possession without intent to sell, or use, is a crime (6 months–3 years' prison; can be reduced to 3–12 months if minor; judicial pardon possible).

cocaine.note: Table I: possession without intent to sell, or use, is a crime (6 months–3 years' prison; can be reduced to 3–12 months if minor; judicial pardon possible).

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely.

alcohol.note: Legal for adults; venues serving alcohol to under-18s commit an offence (Penal Code art. 165).

ghb/gbl.note: GHB and GBL are Table IV: possession or use without prescription is a crime. Sodium oxybate is a prescription medicine.

opioids.note: Heroin and other opioids are Table I: possession or use without an ISS-recognised prescription is a crime.

tramadol.note: Listed in Table I: legal only with an ISS-recognised prescription; otherwise possession or use is a crime.

benzodiazepines.note: Table IV: legal only with an ISS-recognised prescription; otherwise possession or use is a crime.

maois.note: Harmine, harmaline and ayahuasca are Table I: possession or use is a crime. MAOI antidepressants are prescription-only medicines.

ssris.note: Prescription medicines; not in the drug tables.
